topics.label: Introduction and overview of cancer hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session's learning objectives, the historical framework of the hallmarks of cancer, and how genetic mutations relate to tissue-level tumor progression.

topics.label: Deregulation of growth signaling pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how oncogenic and tumor suppressor mutations in signaling cascades like Wnt/beta-catenin, RTKs, Ras-MAPK, and PI3K drive cell proliferation and survival.

topics.label: Blockade of normal cellular differentiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics illustrate how cancers in hematopoietic lineages and intestinal epithelium maintain proliferative capacity by preventing cells from reaching their terminally differentiated states.

topics.label: Resistance to apoptotic cell death
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the molecular mechanisms by which cancer cells avoid programmed cell death through mutations in p53 and deregulation of pro- and anti-apoptotic proteins such as Bax and Bcl-2.

topics.label: Replicative immortality and senescence bypass
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how telomere shortening and cellular stress normally induce p53-mediated senescence, how cancer cells overcome this limit through telomerase upregulation to achieve immortality, and summarize the growth-control hallmarks.

topics.label: Metabolic reprogramming and the Warburg effect
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine aerobic glycolysis, metabolic rewiring across tumor types, and the role of metabolic enzyme mutations and oncometabolites in driving epigenetic alterations.

topics.label: Induction of tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details how tumors switch on new blood vessel growth to overcome diffusion limits for oxygen and nutrients during progression.

topics.label: Mechanisms and biology of metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics analyze the sequential steps, physiological routes, diagnostic detection methods, and clonal evolutionary genetics involved in cancer metastasis.

topics.label: Conclusion and lecture summary
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer summarizes how diverse mutations converge on cancer hallmarks, references recent developments in the literature, and concludes the lecture.
